project.name: dandori
project.description: Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited users cooking for themselves: it plans batch-cooked meals, tracks kitchen inventory, adapts to schedule changes and fills an online supermarket cart. Built in Go with templ, htmx, PostgreSQL/pgvector and Claude.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: Returns a fake LLM that answers with the given steps.

nodes.name: Script
nodes.summary: Adds steps to the end of the script.

nodes.name: Requests
nodes.summary: Returns every request the model was sent, in order.

nodes.name: Asked
nodes.summary: Waits until one request has taken each step scripted, then returns the requests sent so far.

nodes.name: Reply
nodes.summary: A step that ends the model's turn with the given text.

nodes.name: CallTools
nodes.summary: A step where the model calls tools, saying the given text first when it isn't empty.

nodes.name: CallTool
nodes.summary: A step where the model calls one tool.

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.summary: A step that answers with the given response, e.g. to script an unusual stop reason.

nodes.name: Then
nodes.summary: A step that answers with the step the request makes, as a model reads what its tools returned.

nodes.name: Fail
nodes.summary: A step that makes the request fail with the given error.

nodes.name: Overloaded
nodes.summary: A step that fails the request in a way worth retrying.

nodes.name: Hang
nodes.summary: A step that never answers: the request blocks until its context is cancelled.

nodes.name: After
nodes.summary: Holds the answer back until the channel is closed, so a test can act while the model is thinking.

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.summary: Has the model take the given time to answer, as a real one does.

nodes.name: Send
nodes.summary: Answers the request with the next scripted step, recording the request on the way.

nodes.name: LLM
nodes.summary: A scripted LLM that answers each request with the next scripted step.

nodes.name: Step
nodes.summary: One scripted answer of the model: a reply, a tool call, a failure, or a wait.

nodes.name: Call
nodes.summary: One tool call the model makes, with its input.

nodes.name: loop.go
nodes.summary: The hand-written tool-use loop: it runs a brief against the model, runs the tools the model calls, retries the failures worth retrying, and records every step.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.summary: Carries out a brief, emitting every step to the trace, until the model ends its turn without calling a tool.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Asks the model, retrying the failures worth retrying with a growing wait.

nodes.name: runTools
nodes.summary: Runs the tool calls of the model's turn in order, reporting a failing tool back to the model instead of failing the run.

nodes.name: Loop
nodes.summary: The hand-written tool-use loop: it runs briefs against the model, with retries and a turn limit.

nodes.name: trace.go
nodes.summary: The trace of a Run: the kinds of event it records, the Trace that receives them, and the Failure a Run ends with.

nodes.name: TraceEvent
nodes.summary: One trace event of a run: its kind, and the data it carries.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Receives a run's trace events as they happen.

nodes.name: Failure
nodes.summary: A run failing for a reason, with a detail saying more when there is more.

nodes.summary: Runs agent Runs in the background as the User they belong to, records each Run and its Trace, and lets the User follow or cancel it.

nodes.summary: Fails every Run still stored as going, as a crash leaves one, ending its Trace as a graceful stop's.

nodes.summary: Waits for every Run going to end, so a test can read what it left.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Records a new Run of a kind for the signed-in User and carries it out in the background as that User.

nodes.summary: Carries a Run out and records how it ended, storing what it leaves in the same transaction as its success.

nodes.summary: Cancels the signed-in User's Run if it is going, storing it cancelled before it stops.

nodes.summary: Stores a Run cancelled in a transaction, with the document its kind's page tells, and returns the function that stops it.

nodes.summary: The signed-in User's Runs, newest first, without their Traces.

nodes.summary: The stored Trace Events of the signed-in User's Run after a given sequence number.

nodes.summary: Follows a Run's Trace Events from now on, while it goes in this process.

nodes.summary: Carries a Run out with the agent loop, failing the Run rather than Dandori when a tool panics.

nodes.name: Leaves
nodes.summary: Registers what the Run leaves, to be stored in the transaction that stores it succeeded.

nodes.summary: The signed-in User's Run with its Trace.

nodes.summary: Stores a Trace Event with the Run, in order, and sends it to everyone following the Run.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow for the v2 branch with three jobs: check (test database, Chromium for the browser tests, committed templ output, mise run check, and a guard that the browser tests actually ran), changes (decides whether a push touches what a deploy ships), and deploy (builds and pushes the image to GHCR, then rolls it onto the VPS over SSH).
nodes.languageNotes: The changes job diffs the push against github.event.before and greps for shipped paths, so a docs-only push skips deploying; the deploy job keeps a non-cancelling concurrency group so deploys serialise and a stale tip skips itself.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Job that runs every check CI runs: it starts the disposable test database, installs the Chromium the browser tests drive, checks the templ output is committed, runs mise run check and fails unless the browser tests actually ran.

nodes.name: changes
nodes.summary: Job that decides whether a push to v2 changes what a deploy ships, by diffing the push against the event's previous commit and asking scripts/ships.sh.

nodes.name: deploy
nodes.summary: Job that deploys v2 once the check passed and the push ships something: it builds and pushes the image to GHCR, writes the server's .env over SSH, runs docker compose on the VPS and verifies the site over TLS.

nodes.name: Test database
nodes.summary: Starts the disposable Postgres and pgvector test database with mise run testdb, so the suite runs against a database set up the way it is locally.

nodes.name: Install Chromium
nodes.summary: Installs the Chromium headless shell that playwright-go drives, with a three-minute timeout so a stalled download fails in minutes rather than hanging the job.

nodes.name: Generate templ code
nodes.summary: Regenerates the Go code from the templ templates with mise run generate, so the checks run against the current templates.

nodes.name: Generated code is committed
nodes.summary: Fails the job when templ generate changed anything, with git diff --exit-code, so the generated code stays committed.

nodes.name: Check
nodes.summary: Runs every check CI runs — gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint and the full test suite — through mise run check.

nodes.name: Browser tests ran
nodes.summary: Re-runs the browser tests verbosely and greps the log for a PASS, because go test hides a skipped browser test behind an 'ok'.

nodes.name: diff
nodes.summary: Compares the push against github.event.before and sets the deploy output to true when scripts/ships.sh says a file that ships changed.

nodes.name: tip
nodes.summary: Skips this deploy when v2's tip ships changes after this commit, leaving that commit's own run to deploy them, so the newest deploy is the one that lasts.

nodes.name: Build and push image
nodes.summary: Builds the image from the repository root with the commit as VERSION and pushes it to GHCR, tagged with the commit and v2, using the GitHub Actions cache.

nodes.name: SSH to the server
nodes.summary: Installs the deploy SSH key and known hosts in the runner, so the later steps can reach the VPS.

nodes.name: Deploy
nodes.summary: Copies the compose file and Caddyfile to the server, writes the .env over SSH, logs the runner into GHCR, pulls and starts the compose stack, then prunes the old images.

nodes.name: The page is served over TLS
nodes.summary: Fails the deploy unless the site answers over TLS, retrying for about a minute while the app comes up healthy.

nodes.name: 00001_enable_pgvector.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration enabling the pgvector Postgres extension, so the database can hold vector embeddings for matching recipes and ingredients.

nodes.name: 00002_users.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration that creates the authenticated role and the current_user_id() helper reading request.jwt.claims, then the "user" table with row-level security, the own_rows policy pattern every owned table follows.
nodes.languageNotes: A goose StatementBegin/End block creates the role idempotently; the RLS policy compares each row's user_id with the JWT subject, mirroring Supabase's auth.uid().

nodes.name: user
nodes.summary: A User, created at their first sign-in and keyed by their Supabase Auth id; row-level security lets each User see only their own row.

nodes.name: 00003_profile.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the per-User profile table, the first owned table, written when the User picks their Language at first sign-in.

nodes.name: profile
nodes.summary: A User's Profile, holding their Language and the slot times, targets, meal-out estimate, exclusions and appliances added by later migrations, one row per User.

nodes.name: 00004_kitchen.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the kitchen table that records how far each User's kitchen has been brought up to now (up_to) and the scheduler's last beat (beaten_at).

nodes.name: kitchen
nodes.summary: Per-User watermark of the kitchen step: up_to, the last moment reached, and beaten_at, the scheduler's last beat, neither of them moving back.

nodes.name: 00005_slot_times.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding nullable breakfast, lunch, snack and dinner times to the profile, all four set at once; null means the code defaults apply.

nodes.name: 00006_ingredient.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the per-User ingredient table, with its typed name, normalised identity key and nutrition per 100 g, 100 ml or piece.

nodes.name: ingredient
nodes.summary: A User's hand-added Ingredient with a normalised name unique per User and nutritional values per its unit; fibre and sugar are null when unknown.

nodes.name: 00007_movement.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the append-only movement table, the Kitchen Ledger from which Stock Items are derived, with cause kinds and the believed and stated values of a Count.
nodes.languageNotes: The composite (user_id, id) foreign key to ingredient is DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so cascading User deletion across tables completes whatever the order.

nodes.name: movement
nodes.summary: An append-only Kitchen Ledger entry: a signed quantity change of an Ingredient at a Storage Location with its cause; what the kitchen holds is the sum of Movements.

nodes.name: 00008_move.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration extending movement with a moved_to column and a 'moved' cause kind, so a transfer between Storage Locations is one ledger event.

nodes.name: 00009_ingredient_edit.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration granting UPDATE and DELETE on ingredient so Users can edit and delete their Ingredients, still restricted by the deferred movement foreign key.

nodes.name: 00010_staple.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the 'staple' cause kind to movement, so marking an Ingredient a Staple counts each of its Stock Items to nothing.

nodes.name: 00011_portion.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration introducing Portions, ready-to-eat servings with their own nutrition, and the movement_portion join, so one Movement concerns either an Ingredient or a set of Portions.

nodes.name: portion
nodes.summary: A ready-to-eat serving with its own nutrition; where it is and whether the kitchen still holds it follow from its Movements.

nodes.name: movement_portion
nodes.summary: The Portions a Movement concerns, append-only as Movements are, with deferred foreign keys to movement and portion.

nodes.name: 00012_recipe.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the per-User recipe and recipe_ingredient tables, with recipe names unique per User by their normalised key and each Ingredient listed once per Recipe.

nodes.name: recipe
nodes.summary: A User's Recipe with a normalised name unique per User, its portions, slot kinds, appliances and steps.

nodes.name: recipe_ingredient
nodes.summary: A quantity of a known Ingredient in a Recipe, each Ingredient once; an Ingredient a Recipe lists cannot be deleted.

nodes.name: 00013_recipe_edit.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration granting UPDATE and DELETE on recipe, and DELETE on recipe_ingredient, so Users can edit a Recipe by replacing its Ingredient rows.

nodes.name: 00014_run.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the run, trace_event and recipe_draft tables that record agent Runs, their Trace as kind and data events, and parsed Recipe Drafts.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: A User's Run of the agent, with what it was asked, its kind and its status.

nodes.name: trace_event
nodes.summary: An event of a Run's Trace, stored as a kind and JSON data and rendered per Language by the pages.

nodes.name: recipe_draft
nodes.summary: A parsed Recipe document produced by a Run, with Ingredients by name and proposed values, not yet linked to stored Ingredients.

nodes.name: 00015_recipe_draft_delete.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration granting DELETE on recipe_draft, since accepting or discarding a Recipe Draft deletes it.

nodes.name: 00016_targets.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the daily Targets to the profile: calories, protein and fibre as floors and sugar as a ceiling, plus a kcal tolerance defaulting to 5%.

nodes.name: 00017_appliance_kinds.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration constraining recipe.appliances to the fixed list of appliance kinds.

nodes.name: 00018_meal_out.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the Meal Out nutrition estimate columns (kcal, protein, carbs, fat, fibre, sugar) to the profile, with their defaults.

nodes.name: 00019_exclusions_and_brief.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the User's food exclusions, allergies and free-text Planning Brief to the profile, all starting empty.

nodes.name: 00020_profile_appliances.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding a jsonb appliances map to the profile, appliance kind to model note, defaulting to a hob and an oven.

nodes.name: 00021_cycle.sql

nodes.name: cycle

nodes.name: 00022_plan_proposal.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration creating the planning schema: cycle_run linking a planning Run to a Cycle, plan_proposal with at most one pending per User, prep_session, planned_portion and kept_portion.

nodes.name: cycle_run

nodes.name: planning_note
nodes.summary: A User's note to the planner about one Cycle, optionally tied to the Plan Proposal it rejected.

nodes.summary: Goose migration snapshotting the Targets a Plan Proposal aimed at and the soft rules it misses as jsonb, backfilling existing proposals from the profile's Targets.

nodes.name: 00025_freezer_split.sql

nodes.name: freezer_split
nodes.summary: How much of an Ingredient a Plan Proposal puts in the freezer when the Delivery is put away, in order.

nodes.name: 00026_planner_recipe_draft.sql

nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the days a Plan Proposal was judged with, the days before its first Slot and the days it plans, beside its misses.

nodes.name: 00028_arrival.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the document that says what cancelled a Run or ended a Plan Proposal without the User, as a cause on run and an ended_by on plan_proposal.

nodes.summary: Goose migration giving planned_portion its own id and letting kept_portion point at a Planned Portion, so a later Plan Proposal can put the same portion in a Slot again.

nodes.name: 00030_grocery_line.sql

nodes.name: grocery_line
nodes.summary: A line of a Cycle's fixed Grocery List: one Ingredient and the quantity to buy, written when the Delivery is marked ordered.

nodes.name: 00031_put_away.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the put_away_at timestamp to cycle and the 'delivered' cause kind to movement, for what a Delivery put away adds to a Stock Item.

nodes.name: 00032_movement_by_ingredient.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the index on movement by Ingredient, so a Count, a move and a Stock Item page read one Ingredient's Movements.

nodes.name: 00033_plan_happens.sql
nodes.summary: Goose migration adding the Slot a Movement is assumed at and the assumed cause kinds used_up, prepared and eaten, so the Plan happens at its Slots' times.

Turso stays the fallback, and the free tier pausing an inactive project is an accepted consequence.

nodes.name: 0002-go-templ-htmx-frontend.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to build the UI as server-rendered templ pages driven by htmx, with SSE for the live agent trace and a small vanilla-JS island for Cooking Mode, on a Go backend, so the app stays a single deployable binary and a PWA and needs no second toolchain.

nodes.name: 0003-hand-rolled-agent-loop-and-mcp-client.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to write the agent's tool-use loop by hand against the Anthropic API, so every step is naturally emitted as a trace event, with the Go backend acting as the MCP client for a local Playwright subprocess. v2 keeps the loop but drops the MCP client once Cart Fill moved to a browser extension.

nodes.name: 0004-plan-against-known-catalog.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to ground the planner in a locally stored Known Catalog (pack sizes, availability, nutrition) rather than mapping Ingredients to products live at Cart Fill, so Prep Sessions are designed around whole packs and rounding stays minimal. In v2 the Known Catalog is deferred until the browser extension that seeds it exists.

nodes.name: 0005-cart-fill-never-checks-out.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that Cart Fill stops once products are in the user's online supermarket cart and never checks out or pays, keeping the user's money and live store account away from an agent driving a browser against a site the project does not control.

nodes.name: 0006-package-by-feature-with-a-service-per-feature.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to group code by feature (internal/recipes, internal/profile, internal/planning, ...) with three tiers per feature - handlers, a Service and unexported store functions - named by file prefix and checked by internal/web/tiers_test.go, with shared machinery (domain, agent, runs, db, httpx, web, clock, telemetry, apptest) below the features and app only wiring them together.
nodes.languageNotes: The longest ADR: one paragraph per rule about which feature owns a table and which way dependencies may point.

nodes.name: 0007-one-content-language-per-installation.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that every food term Dandori stores or the agent writes is in a single Content Language per installation, set by environment and recorded in the database on first start, because an Ingredient is identified by its name and mixing languages would split one food in two. Superseded by ADR-0015.

nodes.name: 0008-cycles-become-current-on-delivery.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that a Cycle stays upcoming until the end of its Delivery window and only then becomes current, closing the previous Cycle and carrying over what is left, so the last days of the cycle being lived can still be repaired. At most one Plan Proposal is pending, or one planning Run going, across all Cycles at a time.

nodes.name: 0009-boosted-pages-with-fragments-only-to-keep-your-place.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that every link and form rides an hx-boost so htmx swaps the body and handlers answer htmx and a plain browser the same way, with fragments used only where acting on one row of a long list would scroll the user away. httpx.IsPartial is the single rule deciding when htmx wants a fragment.

nodes.name: 0010-settle-the-kitchen-once-per-request.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to bring the kitchen up to now once per request in a settles middleware on every route needing the database, instead of each use case calling planning.Service.Arrive, so use cases read the kitchen as of now without knowing how it got there. Superseded by ADR-0013.

nodes.name: 0011-stock-items-have-no-expiry-date.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that Stock Items carry no expiry date, because the user watches for spoiled food themselves and the Grocery List and the Prep Sessions used to judge expiry differently. Stock is used up oldest first and spoilage is corrected as ordinary drift, leaving a Shortfall replanned only when asked.

nodes.name: 0012-the-store-adapter-acts-through-the-sites-pages.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that the store port acts through Esselunga's own pages in fixed code, navigating and pressing buttons by their accessible labels, while the model gets read-only browsing with no click and no JavaScript tool, so it can neither change the cart nor reach checkout. The undocumented internal API was rejected as an unauthorized client.

nodes.name: 0013-the-kitchen-is-an-append-only-ledger.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that what the kitchen holds is never stored as such: every change is an append-only Movement with its time, its cause and whether it was assumed from the Plan or reported by the User, and Stock Items and Portions held are computed by adding Movements up to a moment, so why the fridge holds 450 g can be answered. Corrections are new Movements, never edits.

nodes.name: 0014-v2-is-a-new-codebase.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that v2 is a new codebase on the orphan branch v2 with main frozen as v1 for porting, because v2's Users, cloud deployment and Kitchen Ledger reach every table, query and page. Code whose model did not change is ported with its tests, the rest is rewritten, and time is an input everywhere, never now().

nodes.name: 0015-users-share-nothing-and-choose-their-language.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that each invited User has their own kitchen and shares nothing with other Users, not even the Known Catalog or Ingredients, and chooses one Language for the pages and for every food term, enforced by row-level security and by the queries. Sign-in is Supabase Auth, invite-only, by magic link. Supersedes ADR-0007.

nodes.name: 0016-cart-fill-runs-in-a-browser-extension.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that Cart Fill runs in a Chromium extension in the User's own browser, fetching the Grocery List from Dandori and filling the cart in the User's signed-in session, so a hosted Dandori never holds supermarket credentials or a live session. The extension extends ADR-0005 by stopping at the cart.

nodes.name: 0017-hosted-on-hetzner-with-docker-compose.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to host v2 as one binary on a small Hetzner VPS in Germany behind Caddy with Docker Compose, deployed by GitHub Actions on every merge to v2, with the Supabase database in Frankfurt. Planning Runs and Known Catalog seeds are long background agent loops, so the app has to stay up rather than scale to serverless containers.

nodes.name: 0018-plans-aim-at-targets-only-hard-rules-stop-them.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that a Plan Proposal is stopped only by hard rules whose breach leaves a Plan that makes no sense or isn't safe (a Slot filled twice or empty, a Portion eaten before it is prepared, an allergen or exclusion, an appliance the User doesn't own, frozen food with no evening left to thaw), while Targets and other soft misses are reported to the planner and shown on the proposal. Dandori does the sums in a check_plan tool rather than the model.

nodes.name: 0019-the-kitchen-ledger-sits-below-the-features-that-write-movements.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to move the Kitchen Ledger out of kitchen into a package of its own, ledger, below every feature that writes Movements: it owns the movement, portion and movement_portion tables, the kitchen lock, the kitchen row and the writes and reads of Movements taking a db.Querier. What was a write up the graph became a write down it.

nodes.name: 0020-appliances-are-a-fixed-list-of-kinds.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that appliances are a fixed list of kinds (oven, hob, microwave, air fryer, pressure cooker, ...) rather than free Food Terms, so a Recipe's appliances can match the Profile's exactly and the hard appliance rule can be checked. A model note stays free text, and adding a kind is a code change.

nodes.name: 0020-faro-a-third-party-script-on-every-page.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision to load Grafana's Faro Web SDK on every production page, vendored and checksum-pinned like htmx and switched on only by DANDORI_FARO_URL, so the browser reports JavaScript errors, web vitals and page translation to the same Grafana Cloud stack as the server's spans. Rejects Faro's tracing package, proxying the reports past privacy blockers, and a first-party collector.
nodes.languageNotes: ADR shape: a context paragraph, then Considered Options, then Consequences; the option taken is the one the title names.

nodes.name: 0021-planning-brings-the-kitchen-up-to-now.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that bringing the kitchen up to now lives in planning, in one transaction that walks Slot times and Delivery arrivals in time order, taking assumed Movements and arrived Deliveries together under the planning lock and then the kitchen lock, writing through ledger.Write. Amends ADR-0013's one step to also take Deliveries as arrived and ADR-0019, under which ledger no longer runs the step.
nodes.languageNotes: ADR shape: a context paragraph, then Considered Options, then Consequences; it amends two earlier ADRs by number.

nodes.name: 0022-dev-time-travel-runs-the-app-on-a-manual-clock.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision that DANDORI_DEV_NOW runs the dev server on a manual clock with a fake Supabase Auth and the /_test/ clock switch, mailbox and fake Auth routes, so a driver jumps time instead of waiting. The fake Auth is a consequence of Supabase tokens being issued at real time, and the routes are mounted only in dev mode, leaving the binary one binary.
nodes.languageNotes: ADR shape: a context paragraph, then Considered Options, then Consequences; it names the env vars that select the mode.

nodes.name: browser-tools.md
nodes.summary: Agent guide to the two browser MCP servers: playwright-brave for clicking through and screenshotting in the user's own Brave, and chrome-devtools for diagnosing styles, accessibility, performance, network errors and leaks. Also covers the dev-server rules around mise run dev, the dev-database backup commands and where trace, heap and Lighthouse files land.

nodes.summary: The rules code review enforces: pages built from the shared templ components in internal/web, colours and spacing as design tokens, pages showing only web.Message strings, glossary wording, htmx 4 markup with a no-JS path, the web_/service/store file tiers, closed value types, wrapped Go comments and test helpers that fail loudly.

nodes.summary: How issues and specs are tracked in GitHub with the gh CLI: create, read, list, comment, label and close conventions, sub-issues, PRs as a triage surface, and the wayfinder map with its child tickets, blocking dependencies and frontier queries.

nodes.name: triage-labels.md

nodes.name: provision.sh

nodes.name: write_env

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Dandori is a meal-planning co-pilot for a few invited users, built on one idea: a dinner yields three portions, one eaten now, one as lunch two days later, one for the freezer. README.md states the product rules that shape the code: planning covers one supermarket delivery at a time (a Cycle), the agent proposes changes and the User approves them, and there is no checkout, the app only fills a cart. vision.md expands the same idea into the milestone plan, so read it to know which parts of the codebase are finished and which are still placeholders.

tour.title: The Domain Language
tour.description: Before any code, the project fixes its vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md defines Cycle, Delivery, Plan, Slot, Plan Proposal, Verdict and Exception, each with its meaning and the words to avoid. ADR-0008 shows how one of those terms behaves in time, since a Cycle stays upcoming until the end of its Delivery window and only then becomes current, closing the previous Cycle. These words reappear in package names, table names and function names all over the codebase, so reading the glossary first is what makes the rest of the tour legible.

tour.title: The Binary and Its Wiring
tour.description: cmd/dandori/main.go is the whole program: it reads configuration from the environment and either serves the app or answers the container's health check, which is why the Dockerfile can call the binary's own subcommand to check on it. internal/app/app.go is the wiring, opening the database, building every feature's Service and mapping the HTTP routes the browser reaches; it has by far the highest fan-out in the graph, so it is the one file that shows how the features fit together. internal/clock/clock.go holds the only place Dandori reads the time, a real clock and a manual one that tests step, and internal/devmode/devmode.go adds the dev-only time travel with a fake Supabase Auth and a mailbox served under /_test/.
tour.languageLesson: Go's context.Context carries the signed-in User and the request span, so handlers take them as arguments instead of reaching for globals, and the database client runs every query as that User.

tour.title: The Pure Domain Core
tour.description: internal/domain is the pure core of the model, the rules of the glossary with no I/O, so every rule is a function a test can call directly. The files here define the nouns everything else moves around: a Cycle with its Delivery window, the day's Slots, a Plan of Prep Sessions and the Portions they yield, and Portions themselves with their Portion Lots. Because nothing in the package touches Postgres, it carries the highest fan-in in the graph, which is why the planner, the ledger and every feature depend on it.

tour.title: The Kitchen Ledger
tour.description: What the kitchen holds is never stored as such. ADR-0013 records the decision that every change is an append-only Movement with its time, its cause and whether it was assumed from the Plan or reported by the User, and that Stock Items are computed by adding Movements up to a moment, so a correction is a new Movement and never an edit. ADR-0019 then moves the ledger out of the kitchen feature into a package of its own, below every feature that writes Movements, which is why what was a write up the graph became a write down it. internal/domain/ledger.go holds the arithmetic in exact tenths, internal/ledger/service.go takes the User's kitchen lock and saves Movements, and internal/ledger/store.go is the SQL.
tour.languageLesson: The ledger store takes a db.Querier rather than a concrete pool, so the same write code runs against Postgres in production and against a fake in a test without a second implementation.

tour.title: Seam-2: The Domain Rules
tour.description: This is the first of the project's two test seams. Seam 2 sits beside the code it tests in internal/domain, where the files ending in _test.go are external-package tests that call the rules as pure functions: parsing quantities, adding Movements up, judging a draft Plan's hard rules, opening a Cycle from typed fields. docs/agents/testing.md explains the whole scheme, with Seam 1 driving the app over HTTP, Seam 2 testing the domain core as pure functions, and a third family of guardrail tests checking the source instead of the behaviour. Reading one of these files next to the domain file it covers is the fastest way to learn what a rule actually guarantees.

tour.title: The Schema in Goose Migrations
tour.description: The schema is the numbered files under internal/db/migrations, applied by Goose at startup from Go's embed, so the database's history has the same shape as the code's history. Read them in number order and you read the product's data model chronologically: users and their row-level security first, then the append-only movement table, then the cycle table whose status is computed rather than stored, then the planning tables with a partial unique index allowing only one pending Plan Proposal per User, and finally the fixed Grocery List lines written when a Delivery is marked ordered. The table-level nodes in this tour point at the same migrations for the individual tables, so a table's meaning is readable next to the DDL that created it.
tour.languageLesson: Goose migrations are numbered files applied once each and recorded in a version table, so a schema change is a new file rather than an edit of an old one, and the current schema is always reproducible from the repository.

tour.title: Every User Sees Own Rows
tour.description: Multi-tenant isolation lives in the database rather than in the query layer: the users migration creates an authenticated role, a current_user_id() helper that reads the JWT claims, and an own_rows policy pattern that every owned table copies. internal/db/user.go carries the signed-in User on a context and runs queries as them, so row-level security does the scoping for free, and internal/db/db.go opens the pgx pool, applies the embedded migrations and traces every query without its arguments. internal/auth/service.go is the other half of the story, magic links through Supabase Auth and the User created at their first sign-in, and ADR-0015 records that each invited User shares nothing at all, not even the Known Catalog.

tour.title: Features as Package Slices
tour.description: ADR-0006's layout seen in code: each feature is a package split into prefixed tier files, web handlers, messages and forms, a Service and an unexported store, with shared machinery below the features and only app.go wiring them together. The Services show what each feature is really about: internal/ingredients/service.go refuses names that are taken and units fixed by movements, internal/kitchen/service.go records Counts, moves and Portion additions as Movements in one transaction, internal/today/service.go answers the day's Slots and how up to date the kitchen is, internal/recipes/service.go is the Recipe Library and internal/planning/service.go opens and drops Cycles. Read a feature's Service before its handlers, because the handlers are thin and the Service holds the rules and the refusals.
tour.languageLesson: Go keeps the store unexported inside the feature package, so the Service is the only way in and the SQL cannot leak into another feature's call site.

tour.title: Planning a Cycle
tour.description: Planning is where the domain, the agent and the database meet. internal/planning/service_plan.go builds the prompt and brief the planner Run is given, judges its draft Plan against the hard rules and stores the Plan Proposal it submits, while internal/planning/service_ledger.go brings the kitchen up to now, decides proposals and starts the replanning Runs. internal/domain/judge.go is the Verdict, the hard rules a Plan breaks, the days it plans and the soft misses against the User's Targets, and internal/domain/grocery.go computes what a Plan still needs to buy against the stock and where a Delivery puts its lines away. internal/planning/web_handlers.go is where the User sees all of it: the Cycle page, the Kitchen Check, approving or rejecting a proposal with a note, and the Grocery List.

tour.title: The Agent Engine
tour.description: ADR-0003 records the decision to write the agent's tool-use loop by hand against the Anthropic API instead of using a framework, so that every step is naturally a trace event. internal/agent/brief.go is what a Run is told, the system prompt, the stable block, the prompt, the tools it may use and the effort, and internal/agent/agent.go holds the port itself: the LLM interface, the request and response, the conversation blocks and the tools offered to the model. internal/agent/loop.go runs the brief against the model, runs the tools it calls, retries the failures worth retrying and records every step, and internal/agent/trace.go defines the event kinds the live trace renders, while internal/agent/anthropic/anthropic.go is the real client over the Claude API.
tour.languageLesson: The model is a port: an interface the hand-written loop depends on, so the real Anthropic client and the scripted test double are interchangeable implementations of the same contract.

tour.title: The Shared Web Shell
tour.description: ADR-0002 records the decision to build the UI as server-rendered templ pages driven by htmx, with SSE for the live agent trace, on a Go backend, so the app stays a single deployable binary and a PWA. internal/web/web.go is the shell, with the static assets, the PWA manifest, the service worker and the Faro collector's URL, and internal/web/i18n.go is the shared i18n layer, the Message type every page shows, the Language of the request and the date, time and number formats each Language writes. internal/web/answer.go is the Answer a write gives, a fragment and a trigger for htmx, a redirect for a plain browser or the page itself, and internal/web/notice.go is the floating Notice carried across a redirect in a cookie. Every feature page is built from these components, so one feature's templates teach the whole UI vocabulary.
tour.languageLesson: templ compiles HTML-like templates into Go, and one handler can serve both audiences: it checks whether the request is an htmx one and returns a fragment or a whole page accordingly, which is why every link and form can ride an hx-boost.

tour.title: Seam-1: The apptest Harness
tour.description: This is the other seam: Seam 1 drives the whole app over HTTP against a real, freshly migrated Postgres of its own. internal/apptest/apptest.go starts Dandori in-process with a manual clock the test steps, a fake Auth, a scripted model and the HTTP helpers the tests use, while internal/apptest/scenario.go turns a test into Given/When/Then over the app's clock and keeps a timeline a failed test prints, and internal/apptest/browser.go drives a real headless Chromium for the tests that need the UI as the User gets it. internal/app/plan_happens_test.go is a good example, checking that the plan happens in real time because opening a page or the beat brings the plan up to now and a dinner's second portion is eaten two days later, and internal/agent/fakellm/fakellm.go answers each model call with the next scripted step so a Run goes the same way every time.
tour.languageLesson: The harness owns the server, the database and the clock, so a seam-1 test only has to say what the User does, and the clock is moved through the test's own switch rather than by waiting.

tour.title: Deployment and CI
tour.description: ADR-0017 records the decision to host v2 as one binary on a small Hetzner VPS in Germany behind Caddy with Docker Compose, deployed by GitHub Actions on every merge to v2, because planning Runs are long background loops and the app has to stay up rather than scale to serverless containers. The Dockerfile is a two-stage build, a Go 1.27 builder cross-compiling a static ./cmd/dandori binary and a distroless nonroot runtime image that ships only that binary on port 8080 with a healthcheck. deploy/compose.yaml runs the app behind Caddy, which holds the TLS certificate and waits for the app to be healthy, and .github/workflows/ci.yml is the pipeline for the v2 branch, with a check job that brings up a test database and Chromium for the browser tests, checks the committed templ output and runs mise run check.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate build-time from runtime dependencies: the builder stage compiles a static binary and the distroless final stage copies only that binary, so the shipped image carries no shell, no package manager and no Go toolchain.
